learning_outcomes.text: Students learn fundamental types and description possibilities of signals.
Students know elementary mathematical methods for representing analog and discrete-time signals in the frequency domain as well as their properties and can apply them.
Through understanding the methods, students are able to fundamentally analyze and interpret signals.
Students understand the sampling process and can apply the corresponding theorems.
Students learn fundamental methods for describing analog and discrete-time linear time-invariant systems in the time, frequency, and image domains and can apply them.

Students can apply the skills acquired in the course in different areas such as control engineering or measurement technology, and are thus able to establish cross-connections between different areas.
Through the basic knowledge conveyed, students are capable of identifying and acquiring further methods and procedures of signal and system theory in the literature.

syllabus_topics: Representation of analog and discrete-time signals in the time domain
Representation of analog and discrete-time signals in the frequency domain (Complex Fourier series, Fourier transformation, power density spectrum, DTFT, DFT, FFT, fast convolution, etc.)
(Impulse response, frequency response, transfer function, Laplace transformation, Z-transformation etc.)
assessment_rules: The final grade is based on a written or oral examination.
